A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the personal characteristics of the entrepreneur, the management of the firm and its specific innovation policies are the key factors explaining the degree of novelty of small businesses’ product innovation.

the degree of novelty of the product is an important variable to consider in the innovation studies, and that this variable should be considered as a dependent variable in the innovation process, not as a control variable.

the personal characteristics of the entrepreneur and the management style of the firm are the main determinants of the decision to innovate, while the organizational structure of the firm is more relevant to explain the extent of innovation, i.e. the degree of novelty of the innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the determinants of small firms’ product innovation are not the same as the ones that have been found in the literature for large companies.
the determinants of innovation are not uniform across different types of product innovation, but depend on the nature of the product innovation.
the factors that explain the firms’ decisions are different for incremental innovations than for substantial ones.
